scope: Independent exact source review and eight finite source-to-machine/runtime/rejection controls, using frozen LLVM23 CLI binaries. No full-workspace or performance claim.
findings: All four changed call sites retain the original callee/environment checks, value_type/llvm_type/result calls, Unit argument erasure and their original fallible ordering. No condition or validation is removed.

Signature parameter order, prepended closure environment, result attributes, calling target and vararg settings are unchanged. Each previously cloned temporary is consumed once at its existing final use.

Model Ty/Arg/Param and the owned String/Vec payloads use value-style derived Clone with no user-defined Drop/Clone behavior in these model types. Moving these values preserves the complete model rather than changing any LLVM optimization.
By-value Copy environment, pointer environment, function-pointer indirect call, Unit erasure and FnOnce cleanup are exercised in source-derived LLVM text and native output.

Six accepted source pairs produced byte-identical complete LLVM machine text and byte-identical ELF executables; all twelve executions matched independent expected stdout/exit values, and each build performed exactly one Verify.

Arity rejection and live-borrow conflict retained complete diagnostic arrays and verification-run counts. Both compiler versions preserved pre-existing executable and machine-sidecar bytes on both failures.

binary_provenance.note: Root supplied the fixed build/source bindings; reviewer independently checked both binary SHA-256 values and exact equality of baseline crates trees. Root retained its earlier stale-target release errors and the successful fresh isolated release build log.
